title: A runtime-authored flow that writes a readonly field as the user publishes clean; the button runs, reports success and changes nothing (flow-update-readonly-field is not run at the save/publish gate)
body:
Filing category: ① product defect (user-visible: a button that silently does nothing).
reach: public entries — package publish (`POST /api/v1/packages/:id/publish-drafts`, from Studio's 发布 dialog in a browser) accepted the flow; the console record button then ran it; measured once on a hosted tenant (`pnpm dev:stack --with-ui`; cloud `ff373e02`, framework `d7c3d44e`).

## Business reason

A leave app's 「提交审批」 button is the one thing an employee clicks. If the flow behind it writes a field the object marks read-only (so employees cannot set it by hand — the natural way to protect a status), the click shows nothing, the request stays a draft, and nobody is told why. objectstack#3425 measured the same silent no-op and added a build-time rule for it; that rule does not run where runtime-authored apps are published.

## Steps

1. Object `el5z_leave_req` with `status` (select, `readonly: true`).
2. Flow `el5z_leave_submit` (`type: 'autolaunched'`, no `runAs`) with one `update_record` node: `{ objectName: 'el5z_leave_req', filter: { id: <recordId> }, fields: { status: 'pending' } }`; record action `type: 'flow'`, `target: 'el5z_leave_submit'`.
3. Publish from Studio (all drafts, `outcome: published`, no finding about the flow). The MCP build door's `verify_build` also passed it (0 errors, 7 flows checked).
4. As a member, open a draft record in the console and click 「提交审批」.

## What happens

No toast, no error; the record stays 「草稿」, its 「更新人」 moves to the member. Server log: `WARN Field 'status' on 'el5z_leave_req' is read-only: the caller-supplied value was DROPPED and the update is being COMMITTED WITHOUT IT — the call returns success …`, then `[automation] run flow=el5z_leave_submit … status=completed … acted=1 … failed=0`.

`packages/lint/src/validate-readonly-flow-writes.ts` (`flow-update-readonly-field`, error) states exactly this case ("a SILENT NO-OP … shifts the discovery LEFT to `os validate` / `os build`"). It is not run by the runtime save/publish gate that Studio and AI-authored packages go through, so the case it exists for still ships.

Related trap measured in the same session: setting `runAs: 'system'` on that autolaunched flow (the rule's own remedy) makes the console button answer `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` "This caller may not start this flow. A flow that runs on its own trigger starts there, or as a sub-flow from a parent flow's `subflow` node." (`packages/runtime/src/flow-start-admission.ts`) — shown untranslated in a zh-CN console. The rule's hint should name what a user-started button can be (a `screen`/`api` flow) rather than only `runAs: 'system'`.

## Expected

The save/publish gate runs `flow-update-readonly-field` (and `-when`) over the package being published, as `os build` does, so the flow is refused or flagged before it goes live; and a flow step that dropped fields says so to the person who clicked (objectstack#3407/#3413 made it observable in the run; the console shows nothing).

Reader who acts: the seat that owns the metadata save/publish gate (`packages/metadata-protocol` author-time rules) and `packages/lint`.
Dedupe: `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue read-only field dropped flow update_record silently` → 32 hits; #3425 (closed, the build-time rule), #24690, #24613 — none covers the runtime publish path.
